tier_reason: No number appears on any page I could open: the README and fmm_artifact.pdf only say the generated FMM shows 'a performance benefit over conventional GEMM'. The IPDPS 2017 paper (the only source of numbers) is hosted on cs.utexas.edu and arxiv.org, both egress-blocked here. The public harness (the test driver emitted by meta/misc_gen.py) does time the generated FMM against a conventional dgemm, and compiler and flags are public, but with no numbers and no CPU model the tier cannot stay above D.

corrections.baseline: Conventional GEMM. The public harness (the test driver emitted by meta/misc_gen.py) times the generated Strassen-like routine against the project's own BLIS-style dgemm (bl_dgemm in common/dgemm/my_dgemm.c, built on the same AVX 8x4 micro-kernel) and prints the effective GFLOPS of both. MKL is linked (-DUSE_BLAS, -mkl=parallel) only for bl_dgemm_ref. Whether the IPDPS 2017 paper also compared against BLIS or MKL dgemm could not be checked.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: icc/icpc 15.0.3 with the GCC 4.9.3 standard library (fmm_artifact.pdf); -O3 -openmp -mavx -fPIC -DUSE_BLAS, linked with -mkl=parallel (common/make.inc.files/make.intel.inc with COMPILER_OPT_LEVEL=O3 from common/sourceme.sh)
corrections.hardware: Maverick supercomputer at TACC (fmm_artifact.pdf; CPU model not stated on any opened page)
corrections.caveats: No numbers were seen: the IPDPS 2017 paper (Huang, Rice, Matthews, van de Geijn), which holds all the measurements, is on egress-blocked hosts (cs.utexas.edu, arxiv.org 1611.01120). The repo's artifact description gives icc 15.0.3 and 'Maverick supercomputer at TACC' but no CPU model, and says only that relative effective-GFLOPS trends should match the paper's curves. The public test driver compares against the authors' own BLISlab-style dgemm, not against a vendor BLAS. It is a research code generator (Python 2.7 scripts emitting C with AVX inline assembly, SLURM/Maverick paths hard-coded in config.py and sourceme.sh). There have been no commits since 2017-07-07. arbenson/fast-matmul is catalogued separately and is a different code base.

notes: Downgraded B to D because no page with numbers could be opened. A retier check to B (or A if the paper names the CPU model) is worth running once arxiv.org/abs/1611.01120 or the IPDPS paper can be reached. Metadata was checked on github.com: BSD-3-Clause (LICENSE text), 12 stars, 7 forks, not a fork, not archived, last commit 2017-07-07, so 'abandoned' is correct. Kept rather than rejected because it is the public artifact of a peer-reviewed IPDPS paper.

tier_reason: The recorded wiki page has no numbers, but the independent tblis-rs README (a Rust wrapper by a different group) tables TBLIS against NumPy einsum backed by MKL and against PyTorch CPU on an AMD Ryzen 7945HX. TBLIS wins most strided and transposition-heavy contractions there. The same page cites the method paper as peer-reviewed (SIAM J. Sci. Comput. 40(1) C1-C24, 2018, DOI 10.1137/16M108968X). No compiler, flags or harness path is given, so not A.

corrections.baseline: BLAS-based tensor contraction (TTGT: transpose plus GEMM). In the independent tblis-rs benchmark this is NumPy einsum backed by Intel MKL, alongside PyTorch (CPU).
corrections.claimed_speedup: Independent tblis-rs README (AMD Ryzen 7945HX, 16 cores, FP64 tensors of shape 96^4), TBLIS vs NumPy (MKL) vs PyTorch CPU. Contiguous: abxy,xycd->abcd 1.90 s vs 2.13 s vs 1.98 s; axyz,ybzx->ab 120.7 vs 207.7 vs 211.1 ms; axby,yacx->abc 124.1 ms vs 29.7 s vs 179.2 ms. TBLIS loses on axyz,xyzb->ab (132.3 vs 63.1 vs 63.4 ms) and on SYRK-shaped axyz,bxyz->ab (96.9 vs 293.2 vs 37.4 ms). Strided (stride 128): abxy,xycd->abcd 2.02 s vs 7.30 s vs 2.10 s; axyz,xyzb->ab 133.1 vs 776.8 vs 204.4 ms. That is about 1.1x (contiguous GEMM-shaped) to 5.8x (strided) over NumPy/MKL and 1.0-1.8x over PyTorch where TBLIS wins (derived from page data). The TBLIS wiki itself claims only 'essentially zero overhead compared to matrix multiplication'.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 145 stars, 39 forks; wrapped by tblis-rs (Rust) and pytblis (Python)
corrections.caveats: The project's own pages (README, wiki home and Research pages) give no benchmark numbers. The numbers come from an independent wrapper author's laptop run (tblis-rs README) that states no compiler, flags or thread settings. There, TBLIS is about 2x slower than MKL/PyTorch on plain GEMM-shaped contiguous contractions and 2.6x slower than PyTorch on a SYRK-shaped one. The wrapper author says TBLIS 'may probably not the best choice' for contractions that map to GEMM. The 200-1000x gaps on batched and trace contractions come from NumPy einsum falling back to a non-BLAS path, so they are not a fair TTGT comparison. The SISC 2018 paper (arXiv 1607.00291) could not be opened (arxiv.org and epubs.siam.org are egress-blocked), so its TTGT comparison numbers, CPU and compiler are unverified.

notes: Kept at B on the strength of an independent measurement plus the peer-reviewed SISC 2018 publication (venue confirmed only through the citation on the tblis-rs README). benchmark_url was moved to the tblis-rs README, the only opened page with numbers. Metadata was checked on github.com: BSD-3-Clause, 145 stars, 39 forks, not a fork, last master commit 2025-11-21 (active). A retier check could fill the paper's numbers, CPU and compiler if arxiv.org/abs/1607.00291 becomes reachable.

tier_reason: Upgraded from C. The README abstract's 'up to 1.3x speedup' over the regular TBLIS contraction is the paper's claim, and the paper is confirmed as peer-reviewed: SIAM J. Sci. Comput. 40(3) C305-C326, 2018, DOI 10.1137/17M1135578, cited on the tblis-rs README. Not A: artifact.pdf names icc 15.0.3 and 'Maverick supercomputer at TACC' but no CPU model and no compiler flags beyond --enable-config=sandybridge, although the benchmark scripts (bin/*_run_1core.sh, tcb.txt) are public.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: icc/icpc 15.0.3 with the GCC 4.9.3 standard library for single-node runs, mpicc/mpicxx from mvapich2 2.1 for distributed runs; configure --disable-shared --enable-config=sandybridge (artifact.pdf, README); other compiler flags not stated
corrections.hardware: Maverick supercomputer at TACC (artifact.pdf; CPU model not stated on any opened page)
corrections.caveats: The 1.3x is a best case ('up to') from the authors' own runs, measured against the same code with Strassen turned off (L=0 runs the regular TBLIS contraction). Per-case numbers, the CPU model and the speedups on the Tensor Contraction Benchmark are in the SISC paper, which could not be opened (arxiv.org 1704.03092 and the publisher are egress-blocked). The code appears to be built on a 2016-era TBLIS code base: the LICENSE is TBLIS's BSD-3-Clause, copyright Devin Matthews 2015-2016. Build instructions configure only the Sandy Bridge AVX kernels, and the distributed scripts assume TACC Maverick SLURM queues. There have been no commits since 2017-07-07. This is a research artifact, not a maintained library; for production use the current TBLIS (MatthewsResearchGroup/tblis) is the maintained code base, but it has no Strassen path.

notes: The claim matches the README verbatim. Peer review was confirmed through the full SISC citation on the restgroup/tblis-rs README (not the publisher page), so the tier was raised from C to B. Metadata was checked on github.com: BSD-3-Clause, 15 stars, 6 forks, not a fork, last commit 2017-07-07 (abandoned).
